acceptance_criteria.criterion: Clicking a column header sorts visible rows by that column
Clicking the same header again reverses sort direction
Clicking a different header sorts by that column (timestamps default desc, other columns default asc)
sortKey and sortDir persist across page reloads via localStorage
Default sort on first load is last_updated descending (unchanged from current behavior)
Status filter and text search continue to work correctly after sorting
Auto-refresh (10 s polling) preserves active sort key and direction
The Actions column header is not clickable and shows no sort indicator
aria-sort attributes on th elements reflect the current sort state

summary: Added SORT_KEY_STORAGE / SORT_DIR_STORAGE constants and sortKey / sortDir closure vars (default last_updated desc, restored from localStorage) inside renderProjectList()
Added sortProjects() helper handling string, numeric (done ratio), and timestamp columns with configurable sign
Added thSort() helper inside buildTable() that generates sortable <th> elements with data-sort, class (sortable + sort-asc/sort-desc), and aria-sort attributes
Replaced hardcoded last_updated sort with sortProjects(projects, sortKey, sortDir)
Updated <thead> to use thSort() for all 6 data columns; Actions <th> remains plain and non-clickable

Added delegated click listener on <thead> in render(): toggles direction on same-column click, resets to desc for timestamps / asc for other columns on new-column click, persists both values to localStorage, calls render(allProjects)
Added CSS rules for th.sortable (cursor, user-select), th.sortable:hover, th.sort-asc::after (↑), th.sort-desc::after (↓) in styles.css after the progress-bar block

summary: All 9 acceptance criteria verified by static code inspection of mcp-server/gui/public/app.js and mcp-server/gui/public/styles.css.
AC1 (click sorts): thSort() generates th[data-sort] elements; delegated click listener on thead reads data-sort, updates sortKey/sortDir, calls render(allProjects).
AC2 (toggle direction): `if (sortKey === key) sortDir = sortDir === 'asc' ? 'desc' : 'asc'` correctly toggles.
AC3 (new-column defaults): timestamp keys default to desc, all others to asc — matches spec.
AC4 (localStorage persistence): sortKey/sortDir read from localStorage on init, written on every click — survives page reload.
AC5 (first-load default): fallback values `|| 'last_updated'` / `|| 'desc'` preserve prior behavior.
AC6 (filter+search survive sort): after render() re-injects markup, filterEl.value and searchEl.value are restored and applyFilter() is called.
AC7 (auto-refresh preserves sort): sortKey/sortDir are closure vars inside renderProjectList(); Router._setPolling(load, 10000) fires within that scope, so render() always uses the live values.
AC8 (Actions not clickable): plain <th>Actions</th> carries no data-sort; click handler guards with closest('th[data-sort]') and returns early if null.
AC9 (aria-sort): thSort() sets aria-sort='ascending'/'descending' on active column, 'none' on all others.
CSS: th.sortable {cursor:pointer; user-select:none}, th.sortable:hover, th.sort-asc::after {' ↑'}, th.sort-desc::after {' ↓'} — all present and correctly placed after progress-bar block.

summary: Reviewed mcp-server/gui/public/app.js (lines 241–449) and mcp-server/gui/public/styles.css (lines 511–526). All 9 acceptance criteria confirmed met. Implementation is idiomatic, correct, and consistent with the existing codebase style. No security issues, no architectural violations, no rework required.

comments.note: searchValue is stored as `.toLowerCase().trim()` in the closure but restored verbatim to searchEl.value on re-render. Users will see their search text trimmed after a sort click. Not a functional bug — applyFilter() uses the already-normalized closure value — but the visible input may lose leading/trailing spaces the user typed. Low impact given the search UX.

Sort header <th> elements are not keyboard-focusable (no tabindex, not a <button>). aria-sort is correctly set per AC9, but keyboard users cannot reach the sort action via Tab/Enter. Acceptable for this codebase style but worth tracking as an a11y debt item.

th.sortable:hover applies only a color change (color: var(--color-text)). A subtle background highlight would improve column header affordance for new users, but this is cosmetic and consistent with the minimal existing table styling.

render() re-attaches all event listeners (filter, search, delete, refresh, thead click) on every sort interaction since app.innerHTML is fully replaced. No memory leak risk because old DOM is discarded, but it is O(events) per sort click. Pre-existing pattern — not introduced by this change.
